name: ALLEN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the OAH, as an administrative agency, does not have jurisdiction over as-applied constitutional challenges to tax statutes because the power to rule on the constitutionality of statutes belongs to the judicial branch, and the legislature did not clearly confer such authority to the OAH.

name: NEWBY, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the statutory good faith exception applies only to Chapter 15A violations, but the federal good faith exception and an equivalent state good faith exception apply to constitutional violations, thus allowing the CSLI as evidence.

name: Justice DIETZ
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Justice EARLS
description: Dissented, argued that the state constitution requires exclusion of unconstitutionally obtained evidence with no good faith exception, emphasizing judicial integrity, a constitutional right to a remedy, and deterrence of police misconduct.

name: Justice RIGGS
description: Dissented, argued that the state constitution requires exclusion of unconstitutionally obtained evidence with no good faith exception, emphasizing judicial integrity, a constitutional right to a remedy, and deterrence of police misconduct.

name: DILLON, Chief Judge
description: Concurred, argued that the Legislative Cap is constitutional because the plaintiff's cause of action did not become a vested property right until after the cap was enacted, and the General Assembly has the power to define when a remedy is legally cognizable without impairing the right to a jury trial.

name: COLLINS
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: WOOD
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: BERGER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that a resentencing court retains de novo authority over unaddressed issues unless explicitly limited by a mandate, and the previous mandate only addressed murder convictions.

name: NEWBY, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the statute allowing mid-deliberation juror substitution with an instruction to restart deliberations ensures the verdict is rendered by a constitutionally requisite jury of twelve.

name: Justice RIGGS
description: Dissented, argued that the statute allowing mid-deliberation juror substitution violates the constitutional right to a unanimous jury of twelve, as curative instructions cannot remedy this structural error.

name: Justice EARLS
description: Dissented with Justice Riggs's opinion.

name: BERGER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court erred in granting summary judgment on the Fruits of Labor claim and that the Court of Appeals incorrectly applied strict scrutiny to the Equal Protection claim, remanding the Fruits of Labor claim for further discovery and reversing the Equal Protection ruling.

name: Justice RIGGS
description: Dissented, argued that the Fruits of Labor claim should be barred by sovereign immunity due to an adequate alternative remedy under the Emergency Management Act, and that the Association failed to provide evidence to establish a disputed issue of material fact for its Fruits of Labor claim. Concurred with the majority on the Public Records Act and Equal Protection claims.

name: Justice EARLS
description: Dissented with Justice Riggs's opinion.

name: NEWBY, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the PREP Act's immunity only covers tort injuries and does not preempt state constitutional claims regarding parental rights and bodily integrity.

name: Justice BERGER
description: Concurred, argued that forced medication is a battery rooted in Lockean self-ownership and that the PREP Act's sweeping immunity seems contrary to this basic understanding, especially for intentional torts not resulting in death or serious injury.

name: Justice BARRINGER
description: Concurred with majority opinion

name: Justice RIGGS
description: Dissented, argued that the majority rewrites an unambiguous statute to exclude state constitutional claims from PREP Act immunity and that the PREP Act's broad language clearly preempts all claims for loss, including constitutional ones.

name: Justice EARLS
description: Dissented with majority opinion

name: EARLS, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that legislators elected from unconstitutionally gerrymandered districts have limits on their authority to propose constitutional amendments, and the validity of such amendments must be scrutinized if the votes of those legislators were decisive and the amendments threaten popular sovereignty or democratic self-rule.

name: Justice BERGER
description: Dissented, argued that the people of North Carolina already settled the question by approving the amendments, and the majority's decision invalidates millions of votes and oversteps judicial authority by imposing policy preferences.

name: Chief Justice NEWBY
description: Dissented, argued that the people of North Carolina already settled the question by approving the amendments, and the majority's decision invalidates millions of votes and oversteps judicial authority by imposing policy preferences.

name: Justice BARRINGER
description: Dissented, argued that the people of North Carolina already settled the question by approving the amendments, and the majority's decision invalidates millions of votes and oversteps judicial authority by imposing policy preferences.

name: TYSON
description: Concurred with majority opinion, arguing that the Board erred in dismissing election protests, requiring a cure period for incomplete registrations and photo ID issues, and disqualifying "Never Residents" to ensure election integrity.

name: GORE
description: Concurred with majority opinion, arguing that the Board erred in dismissing election protests, requiring a cure period for incomplete registrations and photo ID issues, and disqualifying "Never Residents" to ensure election integrity.

name: HAMPSON, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Petitioner failed to identify any ineligible voters under existing law, the Board's dismissal was correct, the majority's "cure period" is a fiction leading to mass disenfranchisement, and changing election rules after votes are cast violates equitable principles and due process.

name: NEWBY, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Article I, Section 27 provides less protection for juvenile criminal defendants than the Eighth Amendment, and North Carolina courts lockstep with federal constitutional analysis to ensure federal guarantees are met, thus affirming the Court of Appeals' decision.

name: Justice BERGER
description: Concurred, argued that Kelliher is an isolated opinion with little precedential weight because its reasoning did not flow from a series of prior decisions and was inconsistent with prior case law, and the Court appropriately corrects course.

name: Justice BARRINGER
description: Concurred with Justice Berger's opinion.

name: Justice ALLEN
description: Concurred with Justice Berger's opinion.

name: Justice EARLS
description: Concurred in the result only, argued that the majority's discussion of Section 27 and its overlap with the Eighth Amendment is nonbinding dicta, and that Section 27's text, history, and precedent indicate it provides distinct and broader protections for criminal defendants than the Eighth Amendment.

name: Justice RIGGS
description: Concurred with Justice Earls' opinion.

name: RIGGS, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that a replacement judge has constitutional authority to preside over a clerk's removal, that removal must be based only on allegations in the initiating affidavit, and that the standard for removal is "misconduct."

name: Justice ALLEN
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: DIETZ, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that North Carolina courts must apply de novo review to state agency interpretations of regulations and rejected the dissent's reasoning on remanding the First Amendment issue.

name: EARLS, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the Court had jurisdiction over the First Amendment issue and that Professor Mitchell's letter was protected speech, and also partially concurred on the procedural compliance but disagreed with the majority's broad ruling on agency deference.

name: RIGGS, Justice
description: Dissented, joined Justice Earls' opinion regarding jurisdiction over the First Amendment issue and the broad ruling on agency deference.

name: NEWBY, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the state constitution does not grant a protected vested right in the running of a tort claim's statute of limitations, thus upholding the SAFE Child Act.

name: Justice RIGGS
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Justice EARLS
description: Concurred in the result, agreeing that the SAFE Child Act is constitutional as statutes of limitations are procedural, not substantive rights, and the legislature has a legitimate interest in allowing victims to seek justice. However, dissented from the majority's 'extreme originalism' interpretive methodology.

name: EARLS, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that administrative exhaustion is not a jurisdictional requirement for direct constitutional claims (Corum claims) and that the Court of Appeals erred by conflating administrative exhaustion with subject-matter jurisdiction.

name: EARLS, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the Local Act and Interlocal Agreement align with the Fines and Forfeitures Clause's purposes by enabling a red light camera program that provides a revenue stream for public schools, treating program costs as reasonable collection expenses.

name: Justice DIETZ
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Justice BERGER
description: Dissented, argued that the majority misinterprets statutory and constitutional requirements, allowing impermissible enforcement costs to be deducted and diverting funds from public schools, contrary to the Fines and Forfeitures Clause.

name: NEWBY, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the absolute privilege broadly protects all individuals involved in election protests from defamation claims, as the privilege attaches to the occasion of the quasi-judicial proceeding, not the specific role of the individual.

name: Justice EARLS
description: Recused from the case.

name: Justice RIGGS
description: Recused from the case.

name: DIETZ, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that dismissal of criminal charges was an incredibly meaningful and adequate remedy for the speedy trial violation, thus barring the plaintiff's Corum claim for additional money damages.

name: Justice EARLS
description: Dissented, argued that dismissing the charges only addressed a narrow slice of the harms from the speedy trial violation and was not an adequate remedy for the full scope of constitutional injuries, and denying a civil remedy erodes the constitutional right itself.

name: Justice RIGGS
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: Justice ALLEN
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: BERGER, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that S.B. 824 does not violate the North Carolina Constitution as it was not enacted with discriminatory intent and does not produce a meaningful disparate impact, and the lower court erred in its legal analysis.

name: Justice MORGAN
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision reflects partisan biases, departs from federal and state precedent, and improperly reweighs evidence to shield the legislature from scrutiny for discriminatory intent.

name: Justice EARLS
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision reflects partisan biases, departs from federal and state precedent, and improperly reweighs evidence to shield the legislature from scrutiny for discriminatory intent.

name: ALLEN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that N.C. G.S. § 13-1 is constitutional as it does not unlawfully discriminate based on race or wealth, and felons do not have a fundamental right to vote until their citizenship rights are restored as prescribed by law.

name: Justice EARLS
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision perpetuates a vestige of slavery by denying a basic human right, ignores trial court facts, and that N.C. G.S. § 13-1 unconstitutionally discriminates based on race and wealth, and violates the Free Elections Clause.

name: Justice MORGAN
description: Dissented, argued that N.C. G.S. § 13-1 is unconstitutional for the reasons stated in Justice Earls' dissenting opinion.

name: NEWBY, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that partisan gerrymandering claims are nonjusticiable political questions because the state constitution assigns redistricting authority to the General Assembly and does not provide judicially manageable standards for such claims.

name: EARLS Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's decision strips North Carolinians of their fundamental right to vote on equal terms, undermines democratic norms, and allows unchecked partisan gerrymandering.

name: Justice MORGAN
description: Dissented, joined Justice Earls' dissenting opinion, arguing against the majority's manipulation of constitutional principles and the rule of law.

name: BARRINGER, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court complied with the statutory procedure for jury trial waiver by personally addressing the defendant and determining his understanding, even if counsel responded on his behalf, and did not abuse its discretion.

name: Justice ERVIN
description: Dissented, argued that the trial court failed to adequately comply with the statutory procedures for jury trial waiver, creating an unacceptable risk that the defendant did not fully understand the consequences of waiving his fundamental right to a jury trial, and that this constituted a constitutional violation.

name: Justice HUDSON
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: Justice EARLS
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: MORGAN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that a criminal defendant does not possess the right to compel the district attorney to reinstate dismissed charges or place them on a trial court's calendar, and that a trial court lacks the authority to order such reinstatement.

name: BERGER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the defendant's jury trial waiver was valid and any procedural error was not prejudicial.

name: Justice ERVIN
description: Dissented, argued that the trial court's procedural failures constituted a structural error infringing the defendant's fundamental right to a jury trial, warranting a new trial.

name: Justice HUDSON
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: Justice EARLS
description: Dissented with majority opinion.

name: NEWBY, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that a school board's deliberate indifference to ongoing student harassment can deny students their constitutional right to a sound basic education, and governmental immunity does not bar such a claim.

name: NEWBY, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the First Amendment and state constitution explicitly protect petitioning activity, including the defendants' speech in this case, and therefore the trial court properly granted the motion to dismiss.
